assessments.tested_scope: ACT versus base activation-direction interventions on the paper's held-out jailbreaks and tested model-specific steering strengths; strongest clean reversal on Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-1.7B.
assessments.rationale: Primary intervention directly subtracts the learned refusal direction from ACT and applies the opposite intervention to base models. Qwen3-8B ACT refusal falls from about 96% unsteered to 1.2% [0.2,6.6] at alpha=10 while base+direction reaches 100%; Qwen3-1.7B shows the same bidirectional flip.
limits: Requires internal activation access and a direction derived from ACT-vs-base activations.
Other tested families show partial or non-clean reversals; do not generalize to every model or activation-based defense.
No black-box/API attack implication and no independent replication.

assessments.tested_scope: Adaptive Adversaries 15-round three-attacker by three-defender benchmark and its discovered-win replay transfer analysis.
assessments.rationale: The study gives a large 3x3 interaction matrix, 78 pairwise-distinct genuine winning turns, pooled-attacker coverage gains of about 1.4-2.2x, and no universal replay winner among 46 unique replay attacks; raw directional replay percentages retain proxy/decoy provenance caveats.
limits: Use the robust non-universal/heterogeneous-transfer conclusion rather than every directional percentage as a clean final-defense success rate.
Attacker axis is frontier model identity/online interaction, not independently seeded trained best responses per frozen defender.
No independent replication.

assessments.tested_scope: ACT versus BCT on held-out jailbreaks with compliant base-model chain-of-thought prefills and post-thinking continuation under the paper's tested models.
assessments.rationale: The same study intervenes on reasoning trajectory. ACT refuses at least 98% of prefilled jailbreaks on every tested model while BCT loses robustness on most; on Qwen3-8B ACT later self-corrects after a malicious-looking open-ended trace and refuses 95%, and refuses all 82 cases when compliant reasoning and first answer sentence are prefilled.
limits: The trace is injected from the corresponding undefended base model with white-box/prefill control.
The contrast is ACT versus tested BCT, not all output-supervised safety training.
No independent replication.

assessments.tested_scope: MADE closed-loop materials discovery, 30 chemical systems over 8 episodes for two Qwen model scales, comparing BASE and episodic REFLEXION with otherwise matched agent/tools/prompts.
assessments.rationale: Matched memory benefit raises stable discoveries 9.82->14.43 and 14.82->21.28 with p<1e-4 while the study also documents reduced breadth and ignored verbal diversification/cap/exclusion instructions. That supports stronger control than advisory reflection, but the worker's proposed machine-enforceable actuator was not tested.
limits: Breadth collapse was observed; predicted sparse-space failure was not directly tested.
No matched experiment compares verbal reflection with an enforceable constraint actuator.
Workshop evidence, two model scales, one materials-discovery environment.

assessments.tested_scope: Fixed-discordant paired binary audit with r=20, sign bet q=0.75, SeqE-Guard cap m=20, plus stated negative-binomial task-cost model; candidate-level rather than arbitrary per-task scalar boosting.
assessments.rationale: Inverse McNemar sampling supplies an exact Binomial(r,1/2) null and Fischer-Ramdas permits query-path boosting under the conditional expectation bound. Comparator arithmetic matched the worker's raw truncated null mean 0.7033378188 and maximal scalar boost b=1.5309913291.
limits: Random total paired-task cost can be high when discordance is rare.
Arithmetic recomputation is not independent empirical replication of a deployed agent.
Validity depends on predictable/frozen audit design and cited query-path conditions.

assessments.tested_scope: General query-path boost g_c(E)=max(E,c) for fixed-discordant r=20,q=0.75 candidate-level null with m=20 and worker deterministic/Markov stress tests.
assessments.rationale: General boosting maps are permitted. Comparator recomputation matched maximal floor c=0.4511525134 and expected null log penalty -0.6772343230 versus -3.0261899991 raw. The routing benefit remains simulation-local and the boost fades as the cap grows.
limits: Query-path-specific boosting need not improve other paths.
The transform does not cure structural long-null delayed-signal collapse.
No real-agent matched experiment or independent empirical replication.

assessments.tested_scope: Fixed strict-commit query path and iid/nondegenerate null candidate e-values with positive lower-tail mass and finite expected absolute log of min(Z,1); adaptive/dependent streams require extra assumptions.
assessments.rationale: Under the stated iid conditions off-query factors below one create a negative average log penalty and exponentially rising later evidence threshold; worker stress tests are consistent. This is a power result, not a Type-I-validity failure.
limits: Asymptotic result is scoped to stated fixed/iid conditions.
Adaptive/dependent streams need conditional-drift or ergodic analysis.
No external empirical replication of the exact agent-facing controller.

assessments.tested_scope: Deterministic sparse candidate starts/expiries and globally summable start prior; proper predictable likelihoods with absolute continuity; outer infimum after each null-specific weighted killed wealth. Gaussian power experiments are local engineering evidence only.
assessments.rationale: The PFA construction aligns with primary e-process theory: killed null-specific likelihood-ratio wealths are supermartingales, weighted initial mass <=1 remains valid, and the outer infimum is pointwise dominated. Finite-memory tail collapse and telescoping start prior are engineering refinements.
limits: Current theorem is PFA mode, not standard finite-ARL e-detector guarantee.
Data-adaptive starts/expiries and unknown-variance transfer need separate validity arguments.
No independent numerical replication of worker Monte Carlo.

assessments.tested_scope: Standard finite-ARL e-detector sum semantics versus frozen-anchor full-prefix candidate wealth inserted only at its nominal split; worker gives an explicit stopping-time counterexample.
assessments.rationale: Primary e-detector theory obtains ARL control from genuinely delayed/start-time e-process aggregation. The worker counterexample shows why full-prefix wealth cannot simply be added at split time without importing pre-split wealth; this blocks naive transfer and justifies separate PFA and ARL modes.
limits: Counterexample rejects the naive construction, not every possible ARL-valid frozen-anchor architecture.
Different capital accounting or normalized delayed process might recover ARL semantics at information cost.
No deployed-system replication is relevant to this theorem-bound result.
